quote: However, it is worth noting that the term ‘nursing privilege’ is not commonly utilized, with ‘clinical privilege’ or ‘medical privilege’ being more prevalent in the field.
Nursing Privilege is a professional status in healthcare characterized by the possession of professional authority and autonomy, facilitating access to essential resources and information.

The term ‘privilege’ often denotes the unearned advantages and benefits that certain individuals or groups possess in society, often attributed to social status, wealth, race, gender or education (Black & Stone, 2005 ).

In the realm of healthcare, clinical privilege pertains to the authorization granted by hospitals or healthcare institutions to healthcare providers, enabling them to deliver specific care services within well‐defined limits, contingent upon their credentials and qualifications (Jansen, 2009 ).
White privilege denotes the societal advantages and privileges afforded to individuals based on their race, specifically white individuals.
Male privilege acknowledges the advantages and benefits those men receive within society solely based on their gender.

The class privilege recognizes the inherent advantages that individuals from higher socioeconomic classes possess, including privileged access to quality education, healthcare and economic opportunities, in contrast to individuals from lower socioeconomic backgrounds (Barak et al., 2010 ).
One enduring example of such privilege, applicable in all legal settings, is the attorney–client privilege (Plush, 2006 ).
Physician privilege also entails the trust and respect bestowed upon doctors by patients and other healthcare professionals (Hatem & Ferrara, 2001 ).
Defining attributes are the characteristics of a concept that appear repeatedly in the literature and are consistently present when the concept occurs (Walker & Avant, 2005 ).
A contrary case represents a scenario that contradicts or opposes the defining attributes of the concept being analysed (Alannah et al., 2020 ).

When nurses are recognized, respected and have a sense of authority and autonomy in their roles, they are more likely to feel fulfilled in their profession and remain engaged in their practice (Cartwright, 2021 ).
